method.name: cancel_environment_depth_gpu_copy
method.description: Cancels a queued GPU-copy request. Returns [code]true[/code] only when the request was still queued and was removed, in which case its callback will not run. A [code]false[/code] return means the request was unknown or had already been removed for copying; the caller must retain the destination texture until its callback runs.

method.name: get_environment_depth_gpu_copy_capabilities
method.description: Returns the capabilities of the GPU-resident environment-depth copy path. The dictionary contains [code]supported[/code], [code]graphics_api[/code], [code]extension_version[/code], [code]capture_time_supported[/code], [code]depth_format[/code], [code]image_size[/code], [code]array_layer_count[/code], and [code]maximum_pending_copy_requests[/code]. The graphics API is [code]&"VULKAN"[/code] or [code]&"UNSUPPORTED"[/code]. The depth format is [constant RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_D16_UNORM], and the expected array layer count is two. Before the Meta depth swapchain exists, [code]image_size[/code] can be [constant Vector2i.ZERO]. Capture time is supported only when both the compiled OpenXR headers and active runtime support revision 2 of [code]XR_META_environment_depth[/code].

method.name: get_environment_depth_map_async
method.description: Requests that the environment depth map data (including the image data) be sent to the given callback for use on the CPU. This can be used for things like implementing your own realtime plane tracking. The callback will be called with an array of two dictionaries (one for each eye), containing: - [b]depth_projection_view[/b]: ([Projection]) The projection view matrix for the depth map. - [b]depth_inverse_projection_view[/b]: ([Projection]) The inverse projection view matrix for the depth map. - [b]image[/b]: ([Image]) The depth map image data. This method should be called sparingly, and definitely not on every frame. First of all, the depth map image isn't updated every frame - it's closer to every 2-4 frames, depending on the display's refresh rate. But, also, the depth map is provided to us as GPU resource that we need to download to the CPU, which isn't the fastest operation. It would be reasonable to call this from a timer that goes off every 1 second, for example. If you need to use the depth map for rendering, it's recommended that you do so from a shader (instead of using this method), which will be able to access the depth map texture on the GPU directly via global shader uniforms, as well as up-to-date projection information for use on the current frame.

method.name: get_hand_removal_enabled
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if hand removal is enabled; otherwise, [code]false[/code].

method.name: is_environment_depth_started
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if environment depth has been started; otherwise, [code]false[/code].

method.name: is_environment_depth_supported
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if environment depth is supported; otherwise, [code]false[/code].

method.name: is_hand_removal_supported
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if hand removal is supported; otherwise, [code]false[/code].

method.name: request_environment_depth_gpu_copy
method.description: Queues a request to copy the next fresh Meta environment-depth acquisition into an application-owned global [RenderingDevice] texture. Returns a positive request ID when admitted, or zero when the request is immediately invalid or the bounded queue is full. This method does not start environment depth and does not transfer ownership of [param destination_texture_rid]. The destination must be a two-layer [constant RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_TYPE_2D_ARRAY] using [constant RenderingDevice.DATA_FORMAT_D16_UNORM], with the active depth image width and height, depth one, one mip level, [constant RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_SAMPLES_1], [constant RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_USAGE_CAN_COPY_TO_BIT], and [constant RenderingDevice.TEXTURE_USAGE_SAMPLING_BIT]. The caller must retain it until cancellation succeeds or the callback runs. On success, the callback receives a dictionary with [code]request_id[/code], [code]status[/code] set to [code]&"COPY_ENQUEUED"[/code], [code]image_size[/code], [code]depth_format[/code], [code]array_layer_count[/code], [code]near_z[/code], [code]far_z[/code], [code]views[/code], [code]projection_display_time_nsec[/code], [code]source_capture_time_nsec[/code], [code]source_capture_time_available[/code], and [code]extension_version[/code]. Each entry in [code]views[/code] contains [code]view_role[/code], [code]array_layer[/code], [code]depth_projection_view[/code], and [code]depth_inverse_projection_view[/code]. [code]&"COPY_ENQUEUED"[/code] means the global RenderingDevice accepted both layer-copy commands; it does not indicate that the GPU is idle. A terminal failure callback contains [code]request_id[/code], [code]status[/code], and [code]error_message[/code]. Failure statuses are [code]&"TARGET_INVALID"[/code], [code]&"COPY_FAILED"[/code], and [code]&"SOURCE_STOPPED"[/code]. Callbacks are deferred to the main thread.

method.name: set_hand_removal_enabled
method.description: Enables or disables hand removal. When enabled, the runtime will attempt to remove the user's hands from the environment depth data. However, this will only work if hand tracking is enabled and the user isn't using controllers.

signal.name: openxr_meta_environment_depth_started
signal.description: Emitted after environment depth successfully starts.

signal.name: openxr_meta_environment_depth_stopped
signal.description: Emitted after environment depth successfully stops.
